chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me via an upraised chain, from Mansur al-Sayqal, who said:

I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) in his pavilion in Mina. He looked at the people and said: They eat the unlawful, wear the unlawful, and marry the unlawful. But you eat the lawful, wear the lawful, and marry the lawful. By Allah, it is only you who perform the pilgrimage, and it is only from you that it is accepted.

key_terms.إسناد يرفعه: An upraised chain (narration chain ending with the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Why is the Hajj of the Shia considered more valid and accepted according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Fadail al-Shia, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the meticulous observance of halal in consumption, attire, and marriage as the distinguishing mark of the Shia, contrasting them with the general populace who engage in haram. This purity of practice is presented as the criterion for the acceptance of their Hajj, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'al-ghuluw' in piety and the link between ritual validity and ethical conduct. The hadith underscores that spiritual acceptance is contingent upon the believer's adherence to divine law in daily life, a core tenet in Ja'fari jurisprudence.
